text: 20.7 SC NA 14.4 11.6 - SC A60 16.3 31.2 7.04 SC A120 17.6 41.1 23.4 Measurement of dielectric properties The electrocaloric material operates by converting electrical energy to thermal energy, in which the terpolymer thin films are characterized by dielectric constant and loss. For the unannealed films, a lower degree of crystallinity and less latent heat releases upon melting were found from the thermal analysis and are consistent with the literature.26 The observation that unannealed samples show lower latent heats of fusion suggests that entropy changes during this transition will also be lower and that the observed electrocaloric effect of unannealed samples will be smaller than is observed for annealed samples. Dielectric measurement of the unannealed PVDF-TrFE- CFE has been studied before and showed a lower capability of energy storage8 compared with the films that were annealed.13 For films annealed at 60˚C, the SC film shows a slightly higher dielectric constant than the ES film (Figure 4a), and the temperature-dependent dielectric loss of both films has a similar value (Figure 4b). The higher dielectric constant on the SC film annealed at 60˚C could be contributed to a smaller crystallite size (Table 1) compared with the ES film. These results suggested that smaller crystallite size will require a lower energy barrier for the dipole orientation and lead to an enhancement of the dielectric constant.13 For films annealed at 120˚C, the ES film exhibits the maximum dielectric constant of 54 at 30˚C for the experiment, which is about 26% enhancement compared to the SC film (Figure 4c). In addition, the loss for the ES film is much lower than the SC film (Figure 4d), where the loss of ES film is 84% lower than SC film at 30˚C. These outcomes suggest that the film prepared using the ES technique and annealed at 120 ˚C may have a greater ability to store electrical energy as well as have a lower energy dissipation during the adiabatic polarization in the EC cycle compared to the films prepared by solution casting. Because solution casted films are more variable in thickness, dielectric constant measurements were completed at three different positions on a film and at three temperatures to investigate measurement reproducibility (Figure S4). The standard deviation for the dielectric constant was found to increase as temperature increased, however, all of the points measured were found to follow the same trend with temperature. 13 DE-EE0009099 Figure 4.
